notes: Spin bowling is the weakest-served form type in this scaffold, and it is worth being explicit about why rather than quietly shipping a thin file. The cricket biomechanics literature is dominated by FAST bowling, largely because the research funding motivation has been lumbar injury in pace bowlers. What spin-specific quantitative work exists concentrates on ball revolution rate, measured with smart balls and magnetometers at sampling rates around 815 Hz - a ball-instrumentation problem, not a body-kinematics one, and entirely outside what a phone camera can observe. The kinematic variables that transfer from the fast-bowling literature (front knee behaviour, trunk flexion, delivery stride) are plausible but unvalidated for a spin action, whose delivery stride and run-up differ substantially. Nothing here should be scored until spin-specific sources exist. Note also that spin bowlers are the group most often scrutinised for action legality - which this app must never comment on, at any confidence. See docs/ACCURACY.md.

bowling.front_knee_angle_ffc.notes: Do not copy the fast-bowling band here once one exists. Spin delivery strides differ in length and speed, and the front-knee mechanism serves a different purpose.

bowling.interval_bfc_ffc.notes: Temporal metrics are the most robust measurement available and would be the natural place to start for spin.

bowling.runup_final_stride_tempo.notes: Rhythm matters more in spin coaching than raw run-up speed, which makes a ratio-based tempo metric a good candidate - but there is no source.

bowling.delivery_stride_length_norm.notes: Expected to differ markedly from fast bowling.
